'''Broadleaf Commerce''' is a [[source-available software|source-available]] composable [[e-commerce]] platform headquartered in [[Plano, Texas|Plano]], [[Texas]], built on [[Java (programming language)|Java]] and [[Spring Framework]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://martech.zone/broadleaf-commerce/ | title=Broadleaf Commerce: A Unified, Headless, And Microservice PaaS For Ecommerce | website=Martech Zone | date=June 26, 2023 | access-date=March 4, 2026}}</ref> Founded in 2008 by Brian Polster, the company is employee-owned and privately held. The platform supports MACH-aligned architecture — [[Microservices]], [[API]]-first, [[Cloud-native computing|Cloud-native]], and [[Headless commerce|Headless]] — and serves enterprise businesses across retail, automotive, telecommunications, and finance industries. The platform is available as [[source-available software]] that can be self-hosted [[on-premises software|on-premise]] or on any cloud provider, or deployed as a fully managed [[Platform as a Service]] (PaaS) through Broadleaf Cloud. Broadleaf Commerce is a Corporate Member of [[TM Forum]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.tmforum.org/about/membership/current-members/member-profile/?id=0015x00002M1YpQAAV | title=Broadleaf Commerce Member Profile | website=TM Forum | access-date=February 27, 2026}}</ref> Its clients include [[Major League Baseball]], [[O'Reilly Auto Parts]], and [[The Container Store]].

== History ==
Broadleaf Commerce was founded in 2008<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.credera.com/blog/|title=Insights Blog|accessdate=October 6, 2019}}</ref> by Brian Polster with backing from Credera Finance.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.credera.com/|title=Management and IT Consulting Firm|website=Credera|accessdate=October 6, 2019}}</ref>

In July 2010, Broadleaf launched the first version of its framework as an [[open-source software]] platform with enterprise and community editions. Broadleaf subsequently transitioned to a [[source-available software|source-available]] commercial licensing model.

On January 1, 2012, Broadleaf Commerce became an independent entity and gained legal separation from Credera Finance.<ref name="auto1"/>

In 2015, Broadleaf was selected for the 2015 Best of [[Addison, Texas|Addison]] Award in the eCommerce Framework category by the Addison Award Program.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.prweb.com/releases/broadleaf_commerce_receives_the_2015_best_of_addison_award/prweb12876744.htm|title=Broadleaf Commerce Receives the 2015 Best of Addison Award|work=PRWeb|access-date=2017-03-06}}</ref>

In 2016, Broadleaf was recognized by [[Texas A&M University]] in their 2016 [[Aggie 100]] list, ranking 44th with an average growth rate of 43%.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://aggie100.com/Aggie100Archives/2016/2016List|title=Aggie 100 > Aggie 100 Archives > 2016 > 2016 List|website=aggie100.com|language=en-US|access-date=2017-03-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170308045210/http://aggie100.com/Aggie100Archives/2016/2016List|archive-date=2017-03-08|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/business/entrepreneurs/2016/11/12/10-dfw-companies-recognized-fast-growth-years-aggie-100|title=10 DFW companies recognized for fast growth in this year's Aggie 100|date=2016-11-12|work=Dallas News|access-date=2017-03-06|language=en}}</ref>

In 2017, Broadleaf ranked 2420th on the [[Inc. (magazine)|Inc.]] 5000 list of fastest-growing private companies in the United States, with a three-year growth rate of 149%.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.inc.com/inc5000/list/2017|title=The Complete Inc. 5000 List of America's Fastest-Growing Companies of 2017|website=Inc.com|language=en|access-date=2017-11-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.inc.com/profile/broadleaf-commerce|title=Broadleaf Commerce|website=Inc.com|accessdate=October 6, 2019}}</ref> That same year, Broadleaf ranked 35th on the [[Aggie 100]] list with an average growth rate of 45.8%.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://aggie100.com/Aggie100Archives/2017/2017List|title=Aggie 100 > Aggie 100 Archives > 2017 > 2017 List|website=aggie100.com|language=en-US|access-date=2017-11-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171115015509/http://aggie100.com/Aggie100Archives/2017/2017List|archive-date=2017-11-15|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.thecwprov.com/story/36721796/broadleaf-commerce-honored-at-the-13th-annual-aggie-100|title=Broadleaf Commerce Honored at the 13th Annual Aggie 100|access-date=2017-11-14|language=en}}</ref>

In 2022, Broadleaf launched Broadleaf Commerce Cloud, a fully managed [[Platform as a Service]] (PaaS) offering.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/services/broadleaf-cloud/ | title=Broadleaf Cloud Services | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref>

== Products ==

=== Commerce Platform ===
The Broadleaf Commerce Platform is a [[source-available software|source-available]], [[microservices]]-based [[e-commerce]] platform built on [[Java (programming language)|Java]] and [[Spring Framework]]. The platform provides extensibility at four layers: data, microservice, [[application programming interface|API]], and administration, allowing development teams to modify any layer of the commerce stack independently.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/products/commerce-platform/ | title=Commerce Platform | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref>

The platform serves enterprise businesses across multiple industries and use cases, including retail,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/solutions/retail/ | title=Retail Commerce Solutions | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref> automotive,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/solutions/automotive/ | title=Automotive Commerce Solutions | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref> telecommunications,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/solutions/telecom/ | title=Telecommunications Commerce Solutions | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref> and finance.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/solutions/finance/ | title=Finance Commerce Solutions | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref> Supported commerce use cases include [[Business-to-business|B2B]] commerce,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/solutions/b2b-commerce/ | title=B2B eCommerce Solutions | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref> [[Business-to-consumer|B2C]] commerce, unified commerce,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/solutions/unified-ecommerce/ | title=Unified eCommerce Solutions | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref> multi-brand management,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/solutions/multi-brand-ecommerce/ | title=Multi-Brand eCommerce Solutions | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref> and [[marketplace]] commerce.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/solutions/marketplace-solutions/ | title=Marketplace eCommerce Solutions | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref>

=== Transaction Suite ===
The Transaction Suite covers cart and checkout management, inventory and fulfillment, customer and order management, and payment and tax processing. It supports multiple [[payment gateway]] integrations, serialized inventory tracking, configurable shipping rules, and customer service representative (CSR) tooling including shop-on-behalf-of functionality and return merchandise authorization (RMA) processing.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/products/transaction-suite/ | title=Transaction Suite | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref>

=== Merchandising Suite ===
The Merchandising Suite covers catalog management, product browse and search, pricing and promotions, and [[headless commerce|headless]] content management. It supports hierarchical catalog structures, sandboxing and approval workflows, and multi-language search via [[Apache Solr]] integration. Pricing options include product-level fields, price lists, currency conversion, and promotional offer types including percentage-off, amount-off, buy-X-get-Y, tiered, bundle, and voucher offers. Offers can be targeted by customer segment, date, specific products, or geolocation.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/products/merchandising-suite/ | title=Merchandising Suite | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref>

=== Microservices Accelerator ===
The Microservices Accelerator for Enterprise Applications (MAFEA) provides foundational infrastructure services for the Broadleaf platform, including a unified administration console, [[multi-tenancy]] management, authentication and authorization, sandboxing, bulk operations, data import and export, scheduled jobs, and metadata-driven admin extensibility built in [[React (software)|React]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/products/microservices-accelerator/ | title=Microservices Accelerator | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref>

=== A la Carte Microservices ===
Broadleaf Commerce includes over 30 individually deployable [[microservices]] that can be adopted independently or as part of the full platform.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/products/a-la-carte-microservices/ | title=A la Carte Microservices | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref> Available microservices include:

* '''Asset''' — digital content and metadata management, with connections to product catalogs and CMS
* '''Campaign''' — campaign management and offer code generation
* '''Cart''' — creation, management, and retrieval of hierarchical cart structures
* '''Cart Operations''' — checkout process orchestration
* '''Catalog''' — catalog management including products, categories, and product options
* '''Catalog Browse''' — orchestration between a commerce application and microservice APIs
* '''Content''' — [[headless commerce|headless]] [[content management system|CMS]]
* '''Credit Account''' — creation and management of credit accounts
* '''Customer''' — customer profile management and segment creation
* '''Data Feeds''' — job management for publishing data to external systems
* '''Entitlement''' — entitlement access management across devices
* '''Fulfillment''' — shipping cost and option management
* '''Inventory''' — inventory checking, reservation, and management
* '''Menu''' — data-driven customer-facing navigation menus
* '''Notification''' — email and [[SMS]] notification delivery
* '''Offer''' — offer management and discount calculations
* '''Order''' — creation, management, and retrieval of hierarchical order structures
* '''Order Operations''' — order orchestration between a commerce application and order and fulfillment APIs
* '''Payment Transactions''' — payment method data, transaction history, and payment gateway interactions
* '''Pricing''' — price lists, contract pricing, and sales pricing
* '''Rating & Review''' — customer ratings and reviews for products and variants
* '''Search and Indexer''' — search management with full indexing and event-driven updates
* '''Shipping''' — shipping provider management, rate retrieval, and label generation
* '''Store Credit''' — integration with Broadleaf's Credit Account Payment Gateway
* '''Subscription''' — subscription management with promotional and self-service capabilities
* '''Vendor''' — vendor management for marketplace use cases

=== Broadleaf Commerce Cloud ===
Broadleaf Commerce Cloud is a fully managed [[Platform as a Service]] (PaaS) offering launched in 2022. It supports deployment [[on-premises software|on-premise]], on external [[cloud computing|cloud]] providers including [[Amazon Web Services]], [[Microsoft Azure]], and [[Google Cloud Platform]], or as a fully managed service with dedicated infrastructure, DevOps support, and monitoring. The platform utilizes [[headless commerce|headless]] APIs with extension patterns built on [[Java (programming language)|Java]], [[Spring Framework]], and [[React (software)|React]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://broadleafcommerce.com/services/broadleaf-cloud/ | title=Broadleaf Cloud Services | website=Broadleaf Commerce}}</ref>
